title: Velora Analytics - POC scoping: latency SLOs
summary: POC scoping focused on defining latency SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), workload sizing, benchmark plan and timelines.
Customer requires p95/p99 targets for both initial response (TTFT) and sustained per-token throughput (TPOT) across mix of short/long prompts and cold/warm cache scenarios.
Agreement to run two benchmark runs (cold & warm cache) with Redwood providing test harness and Velora providing sample prompt set and traffic profile.
topics: Definition: TTFT vs TPOT and measurement methodology
Target percentiles: p95/p99 latency and acceptable degradation
Workload sizing: QPS, concurrency, seq lengths, payload mix
Benchmark plan: artifacts, timeline, success criteria
Infrastructure choices: hosted vs dedicated vs private + KV cache behavior
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark template + pricing sheet (Jordan) - due 2027-03-17
Velora: share representative prompt corpus & traffic profile (Sofia) - due 2027-03-18
Schedule first benchmark run (cold cache) for 2027-03-22 (mutually agreed)
Joint review meeting to discuss results and tune SLOs on 2027-03-25
action_items: Jordan Marks (AE) - Send benchmark harness instructions + ephemeral creds for hosted test - due 2027-03-17
Priya Nair (SE) - Prepare load script (QPS/concurrency configs) and example CloudWatch/Grafana dashboards - due 2027-03-19
Sofia Patel (Velora) - Provide 500 representative prompts, labeled by length bucket - due 2027-03-18
Diego Ramos (Velora SRE) - Provide target production QPS and peak concurrency numbers - due 2027-03-18
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Marks (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood Solutions Eng), Avery Lee (Redwood CSM), Sofia Patel (Velora Head of ML), Diego Ramos (Velora SRE), Lina Chen (Velora PM), Marcus Park (Velora Infra), Anya Ivanova (Velora Data Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (optional): quick note — focus on TTFT vs TPOT and how we'll measure p95/p99, run both cold and warm cache benches, confirm SLOs and thresholds.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we can kick off — Jordan from Redwood here, quick agenda: align on success criteria, define latency SLOs TTFT vs TPOT, agree on workload sizing and bench plan.
[00:12] Sofia: thanks, yep we want to be sure the model is snappy for short queries but also predictable for streaming long generations, so TTFT and per token throughput are both important.
[00:22] Priya: just to clarify our naming — TTFT is time to first token, that measures initial response latency; TPOT we typically use to mean time per output token or in aggregate tokens-per-second depending on framing, for SLOs we define it as per-token generation latency distribution so we can compute tokens/sec as well, does that work?
[00:38] Diego: yes that helps, our app is interactive chat for customer support, typical exchange length is 20-40 tokens but occasionally 500+ tokens for long context. p95 is critical for UX, p99 for SRE.
[00:50] Miguel: perfect, from Redwood we recommend specifying p95 and p99 for both TTFT and TPOT. example targets we often start with: TTFT p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 600ms for short responses on hosted tier; TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token (equiv ~50 tok/s) p99 <= 40ms/token, but these are that starting points and depend on model/quantization and hardware.
[01:10] Lina: ok can we make those ranges explicit for our workload? our current constraint is human-facing chat must feel instant, so p95 TTFT <= 250ms would be ideal, p99 <= 500ms.
[01:22] Priya: noted, that's pretty tight. question: are you planning hosted or dedicated? dedicated with reserved GPUs changes the variance and helps p99 substantially.
[01:34] Marcus: right now we prefer hosted for quick POC but want to evaluate dedicated if p99 tails are bad. also data residency might push us later to private.
[01:44] Jordan: that's common — POC on hosted, bench, then consider dedicated. for measurement we'll run two modes: cold-cache (first request after model or instance spin up) and warm-cache (steady-state with KV/prefix cache warmed). we'll measure TTFT and TPOT distributions under both.
[02:02] Anya: for warm-cache, how many concurrent sessions do you simulate? our production peak is ~120 qps with bursts to 240 qps, average payload ~30 tokens, 10% long form >300 tokens.
[02:14] Priya: good numbers. for the POC we'll replicate a scaled-down mix: baseline 30 qps, concurrency 40, stress to 120 qps for spike test. we'll capture request ids so you can match responses.
[02:26] Diego: what's the sample size per run to get stable p99 numbers? we need statistical confidence.
[02:33] Miguel: we target at least 10k requests per condition; for p99 stability more like 50k is safer if you can run longer. but we can do iterative runs — quick 10k to validate then extended 50k for final.
[02:46] Sofia: ok sounds doable. what about sequence length buckets, we need p95/p99 per bucket, right?
[02:53] Priya: yes we recommend buckets: short (<=64 tokens), medium (65-256), long (257-1024). measure TTFT and TPOT per bucket as tails behave differently. also include cold vs warm cache per bucket.
[03:06] Jordan: measurement plan summary: Redwood provides harness (k6 or Locust script + sample harness that hits Redwood endpoints), we'll provide ephemeral creds for hosted test or a dedicated endpoint for dedicated POC. harness will emit detailed latency histograms per request, and we'll collect traces for outliers.
[03:20] Sofia: for the metrics, can you export percentiles and raw latencies to a shared bucket or a Google Sheet? we want to run our own analysis.
[03:28] Miguel: yes we'll push raw CSVs + aggregated histograms to an S3 presigned link and also post a summary spreadsheet with p50/p90/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT per bucket.
[03:38] Lina: also need to see tokenization differences — some prompts tokenise differently which affects per-token metrics. can you include tokenizer-based token counts in the logs?
[03:47] Priya: absolutely — load script will log input token count and output token count per request.
[03:53] Diego: how do we measure TPOT exactly — is it per token average or distribution of per-token times?
[03:58] Miguel: practically we report both: overall tokens/sec for a request (total time / output tokens) and per-step latency samples from the runtime where available. some runtimes expose per-token emitter timings, otherwise we infer. we'll include both metrics in the deliverable.
[04:14] Sofia: any concerns about cold-starts on hosted — like container spin up adding seconds? we need to define what qualifies as cold for the SLO.
[04:22] Jordan: good point. definition: cold = first request after model load or instance spin up (no warmed KV cache). warm = after steady-state for 3 minutes or after X similar requests where KV hits exceed threshold (we'll define threshold in run config). we'll run explicit cold-start tests by cycling instances.
[04:39] Marcus: what about network variability — our users are global, and region affects latency. can we pin tests to us-west-2 for POC?
[04:47] Priya: yes we'll run from us-west-2 and optionally us-east-1; for initial SLO definition keep tests in your target production region (you said us-west-2).
[04:57] Sofia: about SLO numbers — can Redwood provide examples from similar customers?
[05:02] Jordan: yes we'll share anonymised bench examples — note depending on model size and quantization, numbers vary: a 13B quantized model on A100 has different TPOT vs a 70B on H100. we will include model variant matrix in the template.
[05:16] Diego: we also care about tail latency during bursts — do you support shaping/backpressure?
[05:21] Miguel: Redwood runtime supports smart routing and capacity tiers; for POC we'll show a stress test with and without batching and with KV caching to demonstrate tail behavior. also we'll collect per-instance CPU/GPU metrics to correlate.
[05:36] Lina: what's success criteria for this POC?
[05:40] Jordan: propose success criteria as a combination of functional and SLO checks: (1) TTFT p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 600ms for short bucket in warm-cache; (2) TPOT p95 <= 25ms/token and p99 <= 50ms/token for short/medium buckets warm-cache; (3) Cold-start TTFT p95 <= 1s for first request; (4) System maintains correctness and throughput at baseline QPS (30 qps) with <1% errors. These are negotiable — you asked for tighter TTFT so we can set warm TTFT p95 target to 250ms if you prefer.
[06:08] Sofia: let's set warm TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 500ms for the POC short bucket; other targets as proposed.
[06:16] Jordan: noted — we'll reflect that in the bench template.
[06:20] Priya: measurement plan details we will deliver in the template: test vectors, per-bucket distributions, cold and warm runs, sample size recommendations (10k/50k), dashboards to review latencies, and artifacts (raw CSV, histograms, traces).
[06:34] Diego: timeline — how long from us sharing prompts to benchmark results?
[06:38] Jordan: typically 1 week: you share prompts (day 0), we validate and onboard harness (day 1-2), run initial cold & warm tests (day 3-4), share results (day 5) then extended runs as needed. agreed schedule earlier was first run 2027-03-22.
[06:54] Anya: any security or compliance steps for hosted test? we need data handling guarantees even for POC.
[06:59] Avery: we'll provide ephemeral endpoints and guarantee data not persisted beyond bench duration; we'll also share our security page and SOC2 summary. if you need private deployment we can discuss but that extends timeline.
[07:12] Sofia: ok please share SOC2 doc and data handling note.
[07:15] Jordan: will do.
[07:18] Miguel: one more technical detail — please specify model variants you want to test (e.g., 7B, 13B quantized, 34B, 70B) and whether you want streaming vs non-streaming behavior measured. for chat app streaming is important for perceived latency.
[07:33] Sofia: start with 13B quantized and 34B; measure streaming p95/p99 for TTFT (time to first chunk) and TPOT across streaming chunks.
[07:44] Priya: noted. we'll instrument chunked responses and compute TTFT as time to first chunk, and TPOT as median inter-chunk time and per-token where available.
[07:55] Jordan: final recap: Redwood to send bench template, pricing and sample anonymised bench results; Velora to send prompts and traffic profile; first cold run scheduled 2027-03-22; joint review 2027-03-25. action items in the doc.
[08:10] Sofia: thanks everyone, that's it from us.
[08:14] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

(end)
